001package com.streamConverter.path;
002
003import java.util.Objects;
004
005/**
006 * Type-safe representation of JSONPath expressions.
007 *
008 * <p>This class encapsulates JSONPath expressions used for navigating JSON documents. It validates
009 * the path syntax at construction time and provides type safety for JSON navigation operations.
010 *
011 * <p>Supported JSONPath patterns: - Simple property access: "$.propertyName" - Nested property
012 * access: "$.level1.level2" - Array access: "$.users[0]" - Wildcard array access: "$.users[*]" -
013 * Root reference: "$"
014 *
015 * <p>Note: This is a simplified JSONPath implementation focused on the most common use cases in
016 * StreamConverter.
017 */
018public class JSONPath implements IPath {
019
020  private static final String TYPE = "JSONPath";
021
022  // No regex validation to completely avoid ReDoS vulnerabilities
023  // Use manual parsing for secure validation instead
024
025  private final String path;
026
027  /**
028   * Creates a new JSONPath instance.
029   *
030   * @param path the JSONPath expression (e.g., "$.userName", "$.users[*].name")
031   * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the path is null, empty, or has invalid syntax
032   */
033  public JSONPath(String path) {
034    if (path == null) {
035      throw new IllegalArgumentException("JSONPath cannot be null");
036    }
037    if (path.trim().isEmpty()) {
038      throw new IllegalArgumentException("JSONPath cannot be empty");
039    }
040
041    // Normalize path for backward compatibility
042    String normalizedPath = normalizeJsonPath(path.trim());
043    this.path = normalizedPath;
044    validate();
045  }
046
047  /**
048   * Factory method for creating a JSONPath for root access.
049   *
050   * @return a JSONPath representing root access ("$")
051   */
052  public static JSONPath root() {
053    return new JSONPath("$");
054  }
055
056  /**
057   * Factory method for creating a JSONPath for simple property access.
058   *
059   * @param propertyName the property name
060   * @return a JSONPath for the property (e.g., "$.propertyName")
061   * @throws IllegalArgumentException if propertyName is invalid
062   */
063  public static JSONPath property(String propertyName) {
064    if (propertyName == null || propertyName.trim().isEmpty()) {
065      throw new IllegalArgumentException("Property name cannot be null or empty");
066    }
067    if (!isValidIdentifier(propertyName.trim())) {
068      throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid property name: " + propertyName);
069    }
070    return new JSONPath("$." + propertyName.trim());
071  }
072
073  @Override
074  public void validate() {
075    validateJsonPathSafely(path);
076  }
077
078  /**
079   * Manually validates JSONPath without regex to avoid ReDoS vulnerabilities. Validates patterns
080   * like: $, $.prop, $.prop[0], $.prop[*], $.prop.nested[0]
081   */
082  private static void validateJsonPathSafely(String path) {
083    if (path == null || path.isEmpty()) {
084      throw new IllegalArgumentException("JSONPath cannot be null or empty");
085    }
086
087    // Must start with $
088    if (!path.startsWith("$")) {
089      throw new IllegalArgumentException("JSONPath must start with '$': " + path);
090    }
091
092    // Just $ is valid (root)
093    if (path.equals("$")) {
094      return;
095    }
096
097    // Parse character by character to avoid regex vulnerabilities
098    int i = 1; // Start after '$'
099
100    while (i < path.length()) {
101      char c = path.charAt(i);
102
103      if (c == '.') {
104        // Dot must be followed by property name
105        i++; // Move past '.'
106        if (i >= path.length()) {
107          throw new IllegalArgumentException("JSONPath cannot end with '.': " + path);
108        }
109
110        // Read property name
111        int propStart = i;
112        while (i < path.length()) {
113          char propChar = path.charAt(i);
114          if (Character.isLetterOrDigit(propChar) || propChar == '_') {
115            i++;
116          } else {
117            break; // Stop at non-property character like '[' or '.'
118          }
119        }
120
121        if (i == propStart) {
122          throw new IllegalArgumentException(
123              "Empty property name after '.' at position " + propStart + ": " + path);
124        }
125
126        String propName = path.substring(propStart, i);
127        if (!isValidPropertyName(propName)) {
128          throw new IllegalArgumentException(
129              "Invalid property name '" + propName + "' at position " + propStart + ": " + path);
130        }
131
132        continue;
133      }
134
135      if (c == '[') {
136        // Parse array accessor [123] or [*]
137        int endBracket = path.indexOf(']', i);
138        if (endBracket == -1) {
139          throw new IllegalArgumentException(
140              "Missing closing bracket ']' after position " + i + ": " + path);
141        }
142
143        String arrayContent = path.substring(i + 1, endBracket);
144        if (arrayContent.equals("*")) {
145          // Wildcard is valid
146        } else if (isNumericIndex(arrayContent)) {
147          // Numeric index is valid
148        } else {
149          throw new IllegalArgumentException(
150              "Invalid array index '" + arrayContent + "' at position " + i + ": " + path);
151        }
152
153        i = endBracket + 1;
154        continue;
155      }
156
157      // If we get here, we have an unexpected character
158      throw new IllegalArgumentException(
159          "Unexpected character '" + c + "' at position " + i + ": " + path);
160    }
161  }
162
163  private static boolean isValidPropertyName(String propName) {
164    if (propName == null || propName.isEmpty()) {
165      return false;
166    }
167
168    char first = propName.charAt(0);
169    if (!Character.isLetter(first) && first != '_') {
170      return false;
171    }
172
173    for (int i = 1; i < propName.length(); i++) {
174      char c = propName.charAt(i);
175      if (!Character.isLetterOrDigit(c) && c != '_') {
176        return false;
177      }
178    }
179
180    return true;
181  }
182
183  private static boolean isNumericIndex(String index) {
184    if (index == null || index.isEmpty()) {
185      return false;
186    }
187
188    for (int i = 0; i < index.length(); i++) {
189      if (!Character.isDigit(index.charAt(i))) {
190        return false;
191      }
192    }
193
194    return true;
195  }
196
197  /**
198   * Checks if the path has array notation like property[index] or property[*] without using regex
199   * to avoid ReDoS vulnerabilities.
200   */
201  private static boolean hasArrayNotation(String path) {
202    if (path == null || path.isEmpty()) {
203      return false;
204    }
205
206    // Look for pattern: starts with valid identifier, then has [...]
207    int bracketPos = path.indexOf('[');
208    if (bracketPos == -1) {
209      return false;
210    }
211
212    // Check if there's a valid identifier before the bracket
213    String beforeBracket = path.substring(0, bracketPos);
214    if (!isValidIdentifier(beforeBracket)) {
215      return false;
216    }
217
218    // Check if there's a closing bracket
219    int closeBracketPos = path.indexOf(']', bracketPos);
220    return closeBracketPos != -1;
221  }
222
223  @Override
224  public String getPath() {
225    return path;
226  }
227
228  @Override
229  public String getType() {
230    return TYPE;
231  }
232
233  @Override
234  public boolean isEquivalentTo(IPath other) {
235    if (!(other instanceof JSONPath)) {
236      return false;
237    }
238    return Objects.equals(this.path, ((JSONPath) other).path);
239  }
240
241  /**
242   * Checks if this is a root path ("$").
243   *
244   * @return true if this represents root access
245   */
246  public boolean isRoot() {
247    return "$".equals(path);
248  }
249
250  /**
251   * Checks if this path involves array access.
252   *
253   * @return true if the path contains array notation
254   */
255  public boolean hasArrayAccess() {
256    return path.contains("[");
257  }
258
259  /**
260   * Checks if this path uses wildcard array access.
261   *
262   * @return true if the path contains wildcard array notation
263   */
264  public boolean hasWildcardAccess() {
265    return path.contains("[*]");
266  }
267
268  /**
269   * Extracts the simple property name if this is a simple property access.
270   *
271   * @return the property name, or null if not a simple property access
272   */
273  public String getSimpleProperty() {
274    if (path.startsWith("$.") && !path.contains("[") && path.lastIndexOf('.') == 1) {
275      return path.substring(2);
276    }
277    return null;
278  }
279
280  private static boolean isValidIdentifier(String identifier) {
281    if (identifier == null || identifier.isEmpty()) {
282      return false;
283    }
284
285    char first = identifier.charAt(0);
286    if (!(Character.isLetter(first) || first == '_')) {
287      return false;
288    }
289
290    for (int i = 1; i < identifier.length(); i++) {
291      char c = identifier.charAt(i);
292      if (!(Character.isLetterOrDigit(c) || c == '_')) {
293        return false;
294      }
295    }
296
297    return true;
298  }
299
300  /**
301   * Normalizes a path for backward compatibility. Converts bare property names to proper JSONPath
302   * syntax.
303   */
304  private String normalizeJsonPath(String path) {
305    // If already starts with $, assume it's correct
306    if (path.startsWith("$")) {
307      return path;
308    }
309
310    // If it's a simple identifier, convert to $.identifier
311    if (isValidIdentifier(path)) {
312      return "$." + path;
313    }
314
315    // If it contains array notation but no $, assume it needs $
316    if (hasArrayNotation(path)) {
317      return "$." + path;
318    }
319
320    // Return as-is for other cases (will be validated later)
321    return path;
322  }
323
324  @Override
325  public String toString() {
326    return String.format("JSONPath('%s')", path);
327  }
328
329  @Override
330  public boolean equals(Object obj) {
331    if (this == obj) return true;
332    if (obj == null || getClass() != obj.getClass()) return false;
333    JSONPath jsonPath = (JSONPath) obj;
334    return Objects.equals(path, jsonPath.path);
335  }
336
337  @Override
338  public int hashCode() {
339    return Objects.hash(path);
340  }
341}
